text:
alex: Heads-up 00 — spike proposal: extract tenant cache from the shared sidecar into a tiny tenant-sidecar (per-tenant instance) to reduce global lock contention. Looking for quick feedback before we formalize an RFC.

priya: Short summary?

alex: Goal: remove hot global cache path from session-core, give tenants isolated caches and eviction budgets. Expect lower tail latency and fewer GC spikes.

dan: How do we migrate without breaking correctness?

alex: Migration phases:
1) Shadow-run: tenant-sidecar does reads/writes in shadow mode; session-core remains primary.
2) Sticky-route cohort: traffic for a cohort is routed to tenant-sidecar for reads, but session-core still does fallback reads.
3) Read-cutover: stop fallbacks; tenant-sidecar authoritative.
4) Sweep: garbage-collect old keys and remove shadow hooks.
Each phase gated by metrics and a minimum observation window.

priya: Any consistency windows we should worry about?

alex: For most cache entries eventual consistency is fine. For critical entries we add a short fencing TTL during cutover and run read-before-write verification in the adapter.

lina: Eviction policy? memory budgets?

alex: Default per-tenant LRU with a configurable budget (default 64MB). Ops can bump via a feature toggle. We'll also support soft quotas that emit alerts before hard OOM evictions.

dan: Observability & telemetry?

alex: Tag traces with adapter_version and tenant_cohort. Emit cache_hit_ratio, miss_latency, and per-tenant mem_used. Increase retention for those metrics to 7 days during rollout.

priya: Rollout cadence?

alex: Canary plan: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Hold 24h at 25% for risky cohorts. Automatic rollback triggers if p95 latency +10% absolute or error_rate +1% absolute. Also gate on quality regressions on our eval suite.

deploy-bot: /canary create cohort-slice-7 

canary created (id: cs-174569)

priya: Cost model? Do we expect more instances & CPU?

alex: There is extra instance overhead but we expect token and retry savings from reduced contention. I'll produce a cost projection spreadsheet comparing steady-state and cutover transient costs.

priya: Tests & staging?

dan: I'll own the staging harness and perf replay. We'll run traffic replay with 1x and 3x peaks to validate tail behavior.

alex: Quick helper for shadow-run: 
```
./scripts/run_adapter --tenant $TENANT --mode=shadow --dry-run
```

lina: Ops toggles we need: memory_budget per-tenant, soft_quota_alert_threshold, and adapter_log_level.

priya: Who writes RFC? Timeline?

alex: I'll draft the RFC and attach the cost sheet and perf baseline. Target Wed EOD for initial draft.

dan: I'll add e2e test checklist to the RFC.

lina: I'll write eviction policy note and ops rollback commands.
